condition: chipped lower left porcelain dental bridge with a sharp rough edge scraping the lateral tongue for 3 days
level_rationale: A chipped lower left porcelain fixed dental bridge leaving a sharp rough edge that repeatedly scrapes the lateral border of the tongue during chewing for 3 days requires dentist evaluation for prosthetic smoothing, repair, or replacement before traumatic mucosal breakdown worsens, whereas that sharp rough edge slicing a deep heavily bleeding gash into the left side of the tongue during chewing represents an acute hemorrhagic lingual laceration requiring immediate emergency department hemostasis, airway-swelling assessment, and deep tongue suturing.

The sharp edge scrapes the left side of the tongue during chewing

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + unsourced hard-bite causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact lateral tongue hemorrhagic laceration escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (lower left porcelain bridge chipped 3 days ago, sharp rough edge on the bridge, and scraping of the left lateral tongue during chewing) with a 1-word span difference (22 vs 23 words), orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f3 on the exact same left lateral tongue site during chewing from superficial scraping to slicing a deep heavily bleeding gash keeps every prior fact coherent without adding a new site or event while shifting care cleanly from dentist repair (level 3) to emergency department hemorrhage and laceration management (level 4).
